title: Early farming in the Ñanchoc Valley, northern Peru
summary: Excavations led by Tom Dillehay in the Ñanchoc Valley, on the lower western slopes of the Andes, found squash dated to about 9,200 years ago, peanut to about 7,600 and cotton to about 5,500, plus other plants. Reported in Science in 2007, it is among the earliest evidence of farming in South America.

uncertainty.note: Ages are given as years before the 2007 publication (9,200 to 5,500 years ago); converted as 2007 minus age, without calibration adjustment. Vanderbilt gives the overall span as 5,000 to 9,000 years.

when.display: c. 7200–3500 BCE (squash c. 9,200 years ago; cotton c. 5,500 years ago)

where.modern_name: Ñanchoc Valley, Cajamarca region, northern Peru
where.historical_name: Ñanchoc Valley, lower western Andean slopes; preceramic communities, no state polity

importance.justification: Early dated evidence of crop cultivation in the Andean region.

sources.title: Earliest known evidence of peanut, cotton and squash farming found (Vanderbilt release)
Early farming sowed seeds of massive change

reviewer_note: Least sure of the dates: the Science paper itself was not opened, and press accounts differ on the figures; ages are not calibrated here. The pin is the Wikidata Ñanchoc site, a valley-scale location.
